Fleet debrief

How the boats compared, and what each can improve.

Hover any chart for the numbers behind it; drag to zoom, double-click to reset.

PCC 2026 — tracked-boat comparison (Feb 21–22, San Diego)

  • 42 boats raced five windward-leewards on Coronado Roads. Three had data in Njord: 1044 "Flash", Chomp!! and Mojo. The official results come from YachtScoring; everything else compares those three with each other.
  • Official results (of 42):
    • 1044: 12-16-17-18-26, 18th overall (63 net).
    • Chomp!!: 29-22-29-31-31, 30th overall (111 net), 9th of 13 Corinthian.
    • Mojo: 31-29-38-30-29, 33rd overall (119 net), 10th of 13 Corinthian.
    • Winner: Bayou Hustler on the tiebreak (three boats on 13 points). Race winners: Lifted (races 1 and 5), DanEgerous, Bayou Hustler, Stark Raving Mad.
  • Saturday vs Sunday:
    • Day ranks were 14th, 29th and 33rd on Saturday; 21st, 31st and 29th on Sunday.
    • Mojo moved ahead of Chomp on Sunday.
  • A place was worth about 10 s. Between the tracked boats, each official place was 4–24 s of GPS time (median 10 s).
  • Over the regatta, against 1044:
    • Chomp finished 7:11 behind and Mojo 9:48.
    • Upwind was more than all of both gaps (7:29 and 7:38).
    • Starts: 1044 and Mojo both restarted in race 5 (1044 at +56 s, Mojo at +52 s), so Chomp's starts came out 48 s better than 1044's over the regatta and Mojo's 32 s worse.
  • Side by side, in the same breeze (within 200 m, same leg and tack; the Side by side page has every stretch):
    • Upwind, 1044 gained 131 m on Chomp and 83 m on Mojo, and Mojo 144 m on Chomp. Each time it was height: the slower boat pointed higher and won.
    • Downwind the gains were small (25–33 m) and went the other way: Chomp sailed deepest, Mojo was fastest.

What went well

  • 1044: best upwind of the three (fastest on 7 of 12 beats)
    • The best angle over the ground (about 81° tacking angle, against 88–89°) at the same speed, on the shortest path (34% over the straight line, against 41–42%), and usually on the paying side.
  • Mojo: Sunday speed, and the cheapest tacks
    • Fastest of the three on 3 of 4 Sunday runs and 2 of 5 beats (race 5's second and third).
    • 10–16 s to recover from a tack all regatta, against 16–27 s for Chomp.
  • Chomp: Saturday downwind and leeward exits, and a race 5 lead
    • Fastest first run in races 2 and 3 (by 27–29 s over 1044); out of Saturday's leeward marks at 4.2–4.9 kt, against 3.1–3.5 for 1044.
    • Led the three for three marks in race 5 (1044 and Mojo had both restarted).

Top 3 to work on

  1. 1044: leeward exits and first runs
    • The slowest leeward exits on Saturday (3.1–3.5 kt; 73–108 s back to speed) and the most lost at leeward marks. Sunday was better (4.9 kt twice), but race 5's first gate was 2.3 kt.
    • Chomp gained 27–29 s on 1044 down the first run in races 2 and 3.
    • Next time: drop earlier, go wide in and tight out, and foot to full speed before pointing. Keep someone looking aft for pressure all the way down the run.
  2. Chomp: upwind angle and tacking
    • About 8° wider than 1044 over the ground, and the flattest of the three on Saturday (15.6° heel). With 18.4° on Sunday it led race 5 up the first beat.
    • The most tacks (8–17 a race) and the slowest recovery (16–27 s). Race 5's last beat had 6 tacks, cost 59 s, and let Mojo past.
    • Next time: hold Sunday's heel, tack only on clear headers, and stay in the middle when ahead or after a bad start.
  3. Mojo: starts and side choice
    • Over at the gun in both Sunday races. It sailed on 10–15 s before turning back and restarted at +44 s and +52 s, costing about 4–5 places each. (1044 did the same in race 5: 0.8 m over, restarted at +56 s.)
    • Saturday: right of the rhumb line 78–91% of the time on four beats; on three of them the left or middle paid (44–56 s each).
    • Next time: line sights and a bow call in the last 30 s. If in doubt at the gun, dip back at once. Stay between the other boats and the mark unless the side is clear.

Replay any race

  • Press play or drag the slider. The panel beside the chart shows each boat's leg, speed, heel, distance to the next mark and gap at the last mark at that moment.
  • Worth watching: race 5 (1044 and Mojo both go back to restart, Chomp leads for three marks, then Mojo comes through on the last beat), and race 3 beat 1 (Chomp's right-hand corner).

The takeaways in charts

1044 was fastest of the three on 7 of 12 beats. Each beat is timed against the fastest of the three; the first beat is timed from the gun, so a late start or a restart shows there (Mojo's race 4 bar, and both 1044's and Mojo's in race 5).

1044 sails the tightest angle over the ground. Hollow dot: tacking angle by compass. Filled dot: the angle actually made over the ground; the gap between them is slip. Mojo's is the widest, the pinching signal, though its ground angle improved on Sunday (85° against 89° on Saturday).

Heel: Chomp was the flattest on Saturday; everyone heeled more on Sunday. Chomp's and Mojo's best beats came with 18–20°.

Chomp's tacks take the longest to recover. 16–27 s back to full speed in every race; 1044 and Mojo 10–16 s.

Speed out of the leeward marks. Chomp led on Saturday; 1044 improved on Sunday except race 5's first gate. Hover for the time to get back to speed and the metres lost.

Side of the course against time lost on each beat. Points on the zero line are the fastest beats. Saturday leaned left, and Mojo's right-hand beats sat high. Sunday was mixed: the right paid on race 4's second beat and race 5's first (where 1044's and Mojo's times include their restarts), the left on race 5's last. Chomp's point at 100% right is race 3 beat 1, the 2:24 corner.

The pattern of the regatta (as seen by the three tracked boats):

  • Saturday: the left paid on 4 of 7 beats; Sunday was mixed
    • With only three boats, "paid" means paid against each other. Where the rest of the fleet went isn't in the data.
  • More breeze on Sunday
    • All three boats heeled 1–3° more upwind on Sunday, and runs were 6.2–7.2 kt against 5.1–6.5 kt on Saturday.
  • Offset marks at the windward mark in races 1–4
    • Windward rounding losses include the offset reach, which every boat sails; compare boats with each other.

Head to head

  • 1044 vs Chomp: 1044 ahead in all five, by 2:28, 0:42, 2:13, 0:58 and 0:50.
    • Chomp was ahead of 1044 at the first marks of races 2 and 5; both times 1044 took it back (beat 2 in race 2, the second run in race 5).
  • Chomp vs Mojo: Chomp ahead in races 1–3 by 49, 53 and 87 s.
    • Race 4 was a photo finish: Chomp 2 s ahead by GPS, Mojo ahead officially.
    • Mojo won race 5 by 34 s, passing Chomp on the last beat.

Data notes

  • Official places and points are from YachtScoring (event 50508, 42 boats). YachtScoring's finish times aren't used: some are data-entry artifacts (race 1's last "finish" is the next morning, and others fall after the next race's start). Gaps come from the GPS tracks.
  • Only 1044, Chomp and Mojo had data. Gaps, "fastest" and "which side paid" are among these three only.
  • Speeds are over ground. The logged wind on Mojo and 1044 is the same smoothed model feed; Chomp logs no wind. So there are no speed targets, and the comparisons are boat against boat.
  • Mark passages and finishes come from the course marks for every boat. Njord's own fleet table has no legs for Chomp after race 1.
  • Tacking angles over the ground come from GPS course, independent of each boat's compass. Heading-based slip figures depend on each heading sensor: Chomp's reads about 5° off, and 1044's reads unusually little slip.

Questions

  • Mojo's Sunday speed matched 1044's. What changed from Saturday, and can it be written down so it carries into Midwinters West?
  • Two of three boats restarted in race 5. Was the line hard to judge (a sag, a current, a pin that moved)?

Speeds are over ground. % right of rhumb: share of the leg spent right of the line from the previous mark to the next, looking at the mark.

Side by side

Every stretch where two tracked boats sailed within 200 m of each other on the same leg and the same tack or gybe.

How this works

  • A stretch counts when two boats are within 200 m on the same leg and the same tack or gybe for at least 60 s, starting 20 s after a mark or a tack or gybe.
  • Both boats have the same wind, so what one gains is the boats: speed, and angle: height on a beat (pointing against footing), depth on a run (soaking against heading up).
  • Gain is progress up the course on a beat and down it on a run, from the GPS tracks. The split into speed and angle is from each boat's average SOG and track angle.
  • Watch plays the stretch on that race's replay.

1044 vs Mojo

  • 25 min side by side upwind (9 stretches): 1044 gained 83 m on Mojo (3.3 m a minute): 81 m lost on speed, 164 m from height.
  • 16 min side by side downwind (6 stretches): Mojo gained 32 m on 1044 (2.0 m a minute): 96 m from speed, 64 m lost on depth.

Boat by boat

Each boat's coach's summary; full reports are in each boat's own file.

1044

What went well

  • Upwind: the best angle and the shortest path
  • Side selection: usually on the paying side
  • Race 4's start: the template

Top priorities

  1. Leeward mark exits
    Next time: Drop earlier, go wide in and tight out, trim main and jib on through the turn, and foot to full speed before pointing.
  2. First runs: Chomp gained twice on Saturday
    Next time: Someone looks aft for pressure all the way down, and gybe to stay in the puffs and on the headed gybe rather than holding one gybe to the layline.
  3. Starts: two restarts from small misses
    Next time: Line sights before every start and a bow call on the distance in the last 30 s. Put the bow on the line at the gun, not the antenna: that means the antenna a few metres back, which costs about a second.

From the debrief; the full reasoning and numbers are on the Debrief page.

Chomp

What went well

  • Race 5: led the three boats for three marks
  • Saturday downwind and leeward roundings: the best of the three
  • Starts: clean and on time in three of five

Top priorities

  1. Upwind angle: sailing wide, and flat on Saturday
    Next time: Sunday's heel is the target: hold 18° or so with traveler and mainsheet, jib a touch harder, and steer for height once the speed is there.
  2. Tacks: the most in the fleet, and the slowest to recover
    Next time: Tack only on clear headers or for a lane. Turn slower through the first half, come out low and build speed before height.
  3. Protect a lead, and don't bank corners
    Next time: Ahead or after a bad start, stay between the other boats and the mark and play the middle. Save the corner for a shift you're sure of.

From the debrief; the full reasoning and numbers are on the Debrief page.

Mojo

What went well

  • Sunday speed: on the pace of 1044, and faster downwind
  • Saturday starts: the best of the three
  • Clean tacks all regatta

Top priorities

  1. Starts: over the line and back, twice on Sunday
    Next time: Line sights before every start and a distance call from the bow in the last 30 s. If there's any doubt at the gun, dip back at once instead of waiting for the flag; a 5 s dip beats a 45 s restart.
  2. Side choice: right when the left paid (Saturday)
    Next time: Decide oscillating or trending before each start. On a beat, go with the side the boats ahead are gaining on; if unsure, stay between the boats around you and the mark.
  3. Upwind mode: make Sunday's setup the default
    Next time: Whatever changed between Saturday and Sunday (settings, jib lead, how hard the jib was sheeted, who was steering), write it down and start there. "Speed before height": ease the jib off the inner mark until speed is up, then squeeze.

From the debrief; the full reasoning and numbers are on the Debrief page.

Numbers from analyze.py and fleet.py. Speeds are over ground. Times are local to the event.
